title: Walking-isomorphism lifting test for Joyal fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, inner horns and quasicategories from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the Joyal model structure from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $\mathcal J$ be the groupoid with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, let $J=N\mathcal J$, and let $u_0:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ select $0$. For every simplicial map $p:Q\to Q'$ between quasicategories in a fixed universe, $p$ is a Joyal fibration if and only if $p$ has the right lifting property against every inner horn inclusion and against $u_0$. No surjectivity on vertices is assumed. The right lifting property means the existence of a diagonal filler in every commutative square with the indicated left arrow and right arrow $p$.

source.place: Proposition 1.13, first equivalent condition; J is the full nerve of the walking isomorphism, not a finite freely inverted interval. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Check the endpoint inclusion from the definition of categorical equivalence in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. We have $J_n=\{0,1\}^{n+1}$, with operators selecting or repeating entries. The object rule $k(0,s)=0$, $k(1,s)=s$ defines a functor $\mathcal J\times\mathcal J\to\mathcal J$, since all target hom sets are singletons, and hence a simplicial map $k:J\times J\to J$. For any quasicategory $C$, let $E:\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)\to C$ be evaluation at $0$ and $c:C\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)$ the constant-diagram map. Then $Ec=1$. Precomposition with $k$ gives $H:\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)\times J\to\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)$ from $cE$ to the identity. This gives a natural isomorphism $h(cE)\cong1$: its component at $F$ is the image of $01$, its inverse the image of $10$, and the images of $010,101$ give both inverse equations. For an edge $a:F\to G$, the two triangles of $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ mapped by $H(a,01)$ equate the composites in the naturality square. Naturality follows for every word of edges, hence for the presented category $h\operatorname{Fun}(J,C)$. Thus $hE$ is an equivalence of ordinary categories for every $C$. Since $E$ is restriction along $u_0$, this says precisely that $u_0$ is a categorical equivalence. It is degreewise injective, hence a trivial cofibration. Inner horns are also trivial cofibrations by the model-structure node. Its right lifting characterization proves that a Joyal fibration has both required lifting properties.

source.place: Section 1, Theorem 1.9 and Proposition 1.13; direct walking-groupoid contraction and necessity argument supplied here.

proof.text: Now assume the two lifting properties. First make extension of an exact equivalence edge to $J$ available. The inclusion $v:\Delta^1\hookrightarrow J$ is degreewise injective: it sends a monotone sequence of zeroes and ones to that same sequence. Let $w:J\to\Delta^1$ be constant at $0$. The functor $[1]\times[1]\to[1]$ with object rule $(t,s)\mapsto\min(t,s)$ gives a simplicial homotopy from $wv$ to $1_{\Delta^1}$. The functor $[1]\times\mathcal J\to\mathcal J$ with object rule $(0,s)\mapsto0$, $(1,s)\mapsto s$ gives a simplicial homotopy from $vw$ to $1_J$. The nerve of a product is the product of nerves degreewise, since a string in a product category is a pair of strings; swap the factors to put the interval last. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], $v$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. In the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], it is consequently a trivial cofibration, so lifts against maps of Kan complexes to the point.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.7.13, simplicial homotopy equivalence implies weak homotopy equivalence; explicit contractions and existing Kan model structure.

proof.text: For any quasicategory $D$, the map $D\to *$ is an isofibration in the explicit sense of [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]: inner horns fill, and the sole base equivalence lifts at each vertex to its identity. That node gives a Kan fibration $D^\simeq\to *$, so its core is Kan. Let $e:p(x)\to y$ be an equivalence edge in $Q'$. This edge belongs to $(Q')^\simeq$, because its other edge restrictions are degenerate identities. Step 2 extends the prescribed map $\Delta^1\to(Q')^\simeq$ along $v$ to $g:J\to(Q')^\simeq$, whose restriction to $01$ is exactly $e$. Lift the square with left arrow $u_0$, top vertex $x$, and bottom map $g$, using the assumption on $p$. The resulting $\widetilde g:J\to Q$ has $\widetilde g(01)$ starting at $x$ and mapping exactly to $e$. It is an equivalence: the images of $10,010,101$ give its inverse and both inverse triangles. Together with inner-horn lifting, this says that $p$ is an isofibration as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation].

source.place: Proposition 1.13; passage from walking-isomorphism lifting to exact equivalence-edge lifting, using Step 2 and the independent core theorem.

proof.text: Since $p$ lifts every inner horn inclusion by assumption, Step 3 shows that $p$ satisfies both conditions of clause (1) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations]: it has the right lifting property against every $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, and for every vertex $x$ of $Q$ and every equivalence edge $e:p(x)\to y$ of $Q'$ there is an equivalence edge $\widetilde e:x\to\widetilde y$ of $Q$ with $p(\widetilde e)=e$, namely $\widetilde g(01)$. The quasicategories $Q,Q'$ lie in one universe, as that clause requires. Its conclusion is that $p$ is a Joyal fibration, which completes the converse. No preimages of arbitrary vertices of $Q'$ have been chosen.
